# mcp

`rea-mcp.json` is what `llama-server --mcp-servers-config` reads. The format is the one Cursor uses:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "rea": {
      "command": "C:/…/node.exe",
      "args": ["C:/…/rea-agents/scripts/rea.mjs", "mcp"],
      "env": { "JAVA_HOME": "…", "GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR": "…" },
      "timeout_ms": 450000
    }
  }
}
```

`llama-server` spawns it once at startup to list its tools, stops it, and respawns it per call, so
the tools survive without a daemon. They surface as `rea_*` on `GET /tools` and in the Web UI's tool
picker.

**Do not edit this file by hand.** `bin/llm-mcp.ps1` writes it from what is actually installed:

```powershell
.\bin\llm-mcp.ps1 -Print     # resolve and show, write nothing
.\bin\llm-mcp.ps1            # rewrite this file
.\bin\llm-mcp.ps1 -OutFile "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\Local-LLM-Project\llama.cpp\mcp\rea-mcp.json"
```

Why it is generated: every value is an absolute path, and a path that moved is indistinguishable from
"the tools disappeared". The script reports anything it cannot resolve instead of writing a config
that fails at startup.

| field | why it is set the way it is |
|---|---|
| `command` | the Node.js that runs REA; forward slashes because a single backslash is a JSON escape |
| `args` | the installed `rea.mjs` plus `mcp` (stdio transport). Pointed at the install, not `npx`, which would re-download on every cold call |
| `env.JAVA_HOME` | JDK 21, kept beside Ghidra in `~/.toolchains`; the machine's global `JAVA_HOME` is a newer JDK that Ghidra was not built for |
| `env.GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` | the unpacked Ghidra 12.x, for the native provider. Without it every non-native tool still works |
| `env.REA_MCP_*_SCHEMA_PROFILE` | `compact` — the advertised schemas shrink; the results do not |
| `env.REA_MCP_TOOL_FAMILIES` | `session,enhanced` — see below. This is a context budget, not cosmetics |
| `timeout_ms` | 450 s. A cold Ghidra start is allowed 330 s, plus the operation. Shorter kills the first analysis |

**The scope is a context cost.** Every tool a chat selects has its schema embedded in the request,
and REA publishes 255 of them — 85 098 prompt tokens, more than `coder36`'s whole 32 768-token window.
So the file narrows the catalog with `REA_MCP_TOOL_FAMILIES`, and the default is
`session,enhanced` (39 tools, 12 402 tokens): `session` carries `open_binary`/`binary_session`,
`enhanced` carries `analyze_function`, `decompile_all`, `batch_decompile`, `binary_overview`,
`get_call_graph`, `find_xrefs` and the `trace_*` family.

```powershell
.\bin\llm-mcp.ps1 -Families session,direct,enhanced   # wider (80 tools, 16 035 tokens)
.\bin\llm-mcp.ps1 -Full                               # everything, 85 098 tokens - only gemma4 can
.\bin\llm-ctxfit.ps1                                  # does the scope fit each preset?
```

Out-of-scope tools are simply absent from `GET /tools`; re-run the script to change the scope, then
restart the server, which reads this file once. Valid family ids (18):
`direct, enhanced, native, artifact, managed, firmware, android, pcap, flutter, frida, apktool, jeb,
adb, browser, electron, javascript-runtime, application, session`.
